title: What if every Ivy League university became public?
narrator: Deadpan documentary: calm and dry, treats the impossible premise like a serious report. The jokes land through understatement.
logline: All 8 Ivies become state schools. On paper, a lot changes. In person, mostly the license plates.

cues.onScreen: What if the Ivy League went public?
cues.narration: What if the Ivy League went public?

cues.onScreen: There are eight Ivy League schools.
cues.narration: There are 8 Ivy League schools, Brown to Yale.

cues.onScreen: All private. All old. All very hard to get into.
cues.narration: All private. All old. Very good at saying no.

cues.onScreen: Then each state takes control of its Ivy.
cues.narration: Then each state takes over its Ivy. The ivy stays.

cues.onScreen: Eight iron gates swing open at once.
cues.narration: 8 gates open at once. New signs go up: state-run. Cornell, which already has state-supported colleges, shrugs.

cues.onScreen: And the line outside starts to grow.
cues.narration: And the line outside gets long. Very long.

cues.onScreen: Problem 1: The tour line wraps around the block.
cues.narration: Open house: the tour line wraps around the block. Twice.

cues.onScreen: Problem 2: Lawmakers now vote on their budgets.
cues.narration: Budget day: Princeton's budget now goes through the New Jersey legislature.

cues.onScreen: Problem 3: Public doesn't mean free. Surprise!
cues.narration: First bill: public doesn't mean free. Ask anyone from out of state.

cues.onScreen: So the Ivies grow to fit everyone.
cues.narration: Biggest change you can see? Parking lot license plates.
cues.delivery: Light; the visual should show the lot filling with in-state plates.

cues.onScreen: Would you still want to go?
cues.narration: Would you still want to go?
